## Remove telnet Clients

The telnet client allows users to start connections to other systems via
the telnet protocol.

**Rationale:**

The `telnet` protocol is insecure and unencrypted. The use
of an unencrypted transmission medium could allow an unauthorized user
to steal credentials. The `ssh` package provides an
encrypted session and stronger security and is included in Ubuntu 24.04.

steps.name: Remove telnet Clients
steps.shell:
# CAUTION: This remediation script will remove inetutils-telnet
# from the system, and may remove any packages
# that depend on inetutils-telnet. Execute this
# remediation AFTER testing on a non-production
# system!


# check wether the package is virtual: if not, remove it.
# if the package is virtual, iterate on providers
#  if a provider is installed, remove it
is_virtual=`apt-cache showpkg "inetutils-telnet" | grep -Pzc 'Versions: \n\n'`
if [ $is_virtual = 1 ]; then
    rprovides_line=`apt-cache showpkg "inetutils-telnet" | grep -n 'Reverse Provides:' | cut -f1 -d:`
    pkglist=`apt-cache showpkg "inetutils-telnet" | tail -n +$(($rprovides_line + 1)) | cut -f1 -d' '`
    for package in $pkglist; do
        not_installed=`apt-cache policy $package | grep -c 'Installed: (none)'`
	if [ $not_installed = 0 ]; then
	    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=60 remove -y $package
	fi
    done
else
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=60 remove -y "inetutils-telnet"
fi
